question: Which explanation of insulin regulation of blood glucose is scientifically accurate?
options: Insulin acts only on the brain and has no effect on muscle or fat.
Glucagon and insulin both lower blood glucose after a meal.
Insulin lowers blood glucose by promoting glucose uptake and storage.
Insulin raises blood glucose by stimulating glucose release from the liver.
gold_answer: Insulin lowers blood glucose by promoting glucose uptake and storage.
notes: Team-authored original item on insulin regulation of blood glucose. Passages are team-authored derivations recorded under sciclaim-appx-A. Requires independent annotation and adjudication before any gate result is reported.

positions.answer: Insulin lowers blood glucose by promoting glucose uptake and storage.

claims.text: Pancreatic beta cells release insulin when blood glucose rises.

evidence.text: Rising blood glucose stimulates pancreatic beta cells to secrete insulin into the bloodstream.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Type 1 diabetes is caused by insulin resistance in muscle tissue.

evidence.text: Type 1 diabetes results from autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing beta cells, leaving little insulin to act.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage identifies beta-cell loss, not muscle resistance, as the cause, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Insulin pumps eliminate hypoglycaemia in all users.

evidence.text: Pump users logged hypoglycaemic episodes alongside sensor readings during the study period.

claims.verdict_rationale: Logging episodes does not show elimination in all users, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Insulin acts only on the brain and has no effect on muscle or fat.

claims.text: Insulin promotes glucose uptake into muscle and fat cells.

evidence.text: Insulin signaling moves glucose transporters to the surface of muscle and fat cells, increasing glucose entry.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states that insulin signaling increases glucose entry into muscle and fat, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Insulin secretion increases during fasting and starvation.

evidence.text: During fasting, insulin secretion falls while glucagon rises to maintain blood glucose from stored fuels.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states insulin falls during fasting, the opposite of the claim, so the claim is refuted.

claims.text: A new insulin analogue controls glucose better than all existing insulins in every patient.

evidence.text: The trial compared the new analogue with one existing insulin for change in average glucose over six months.

claims.verdict_rationale: One comparator and one outcome cannot support superiority over all insulins in every patient, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Glucagon and insulin both lower blood glucose after a meal.

claims.text: Insulin stimulates the liver to store glucose as glycogen.

evidence.text: In the liver, insulin activates glycogen synthesis, converting incoming glucose into stored glycogen.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes insulin-driven glycogen synthesis, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Insulin stimulates the liver to break down glycogen into glucose.

evidence.text: Glycogen breakdown in the liver is driven by glucagon and adrenaline, while insulin suppresses it and favors storage.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage assigns glycogen breakdown to other hormones and says insulin suppresses it, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Dietary chromium supplements cure insulin resistance.

evidence.text: Chromium intake was recorded as a dietary variable in the observational cohort.

claims.verdict_rationale: Merely recording intake establishes nothing about cures, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.
